clue.text: Polo on TV giving you a lift?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the car comes after the television word

parts.note: cable is a kind of television service delivered by wire
the Polo is a small Volkswagen model, so a car

explanation.surface: A question about whether Polo shown on television might cheer you up.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo looks like the sport or the mint; it is the VW car. 'Giving you a lift' is the definition, read literally: a cable car lifts you up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car carries passengers up slopes, literally raising them.

clue.text: What Advent is? In one sense no longer

definitions.text: What Advent is? In one sense no longer

parts.words: What Advent is? In one sense no longer
parts.note: Advent comes from Latin for an arrival; the season before Christmas is an arrival on its way, and one older sense of the arrival word is obsolete

explanation.walkthrough: Advent is Latin 'adventus', an arrival; the season names an event still on its way. The second sentence admits that one sense of the answer has fallen out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means arrival, an event approaching or drawing near.

clue.text: Support clergy taking a stand in front of this?

definitions.text: taking a stand in front of this?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
'the cloth' is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Backing the clergy as they make a moral stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a stand' suggests protest; in the theatre actors take their stand in front of the painted backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted curtain hung at the rear of a stage, behind the performers.

clue.text: Obliteration certain, after a long time

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed after the long period

parts.note: an era is a long period of history
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Destruction is guaranteed once enough years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out or deleting something is its obliteration.

clue.text: Comprehensively exhausted?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both inclusive of everything and utterly tired.

clue.text: Do as English doctor getting on boat?

definitions.text: Do as English doctor getting on boat?

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: Copying a British physician who is boarding a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: to do what someone getting on a boat does. 'Getting on' also tells you the boat follows the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship, which is what a boarding passenger does.

clue.text: Contemplate taking time to act as go-between

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the time letter is removed from the thinking word

parts.note: to meditate is to contemplate

explanation.surface: Thinking things over before stepping in as an intermediary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking time' sounds like adding T, but it means taking T away.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to intervene between parties to settle a dispute.

clue.text: Aged about fifty-four, and still surviving

indicators.note: about means going round, so the abbreviation for aged surrounds the number

parts.note: ae (aetatis) is the Latin abbreviation for aged, seen on tombstones
LIV is fifty-four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone in their mid-fifties who is still going strong.
explanation.walkthrough: AE, the tombstone abbreviation for 'aged', goes round LIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surviving is living, not dead.

clue.text: Resources ensuring entry to Yale?

parts.note: Yale is a brand of lock, so the funds that buy access through a locked door are meant, not university fees

explanation.walkthrough: Yale suggests the university; it is a lock maker. Key money is a payment a new tenant makes to get the keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Key money is a payment demanded from a tenant in return for being allowed to take up a lease.

clue.text: Ropey sort of window-opener

parts.note: ropey usually means poor quality, but here it means made of rope: the line that lifts a sliding window

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropey' is British slang for shoddy; read literally it means rope-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash cord is the rope running over a pulley that counterweights a vertically sliding window.

clue.text: Flower, as girl at end of term

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed at the end of the term's name

parts.note: Michaelmas is the autumn term at Oxford, Cambridge and some schools
Daisy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl appearing as a flower when term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas, the feast of St Michael on 29 September, names the British autumn academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: This aster blooms in autumn around the feast of St Michael.

clue.text: Short Chopin work in part of service

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the piano piece loses its final letter

parts.note: Chopin wrote many nocturnes for piano

explanation.surface: A brief Chopin piece played during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last E from NOCTURNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of the night office of matins in the Catholic liturgy.

clue.text: What about prayer in House? This suggests dismissal

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for what is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is an interjection meaning what?
the Ave Maria is a prayer

explanation.surface: Questioning why there is prayer in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like Parliament, where prayers open each sitting; here it is just the abbreviation HO, and 'in' merely joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the push is to get rid of them, as in the phrase 'give someone the heave-ho'.

clue.text: See me at door turning into passage

indicators.note: turning means the letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be met at the door as they go along a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a corridor; it is a passage of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical passage may be marked moderato, at a moderate tempo.

clue.text: A fellow good at foreign language? That's rich

parts.note: a fluent speaker is good at a language

explanation.surface: A man who speaks other languages well is wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, with plenty of money.

clue.text: Female, English, one in London college

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the college letters

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman studying at a college in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a woman's name, so a female.

clue.text: If sidecar's damaged it's only scratched superficially

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A motorbike sidecar only received surface scratches.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarify is to make shallow cuts in the skin or soil.

clue.text: Distant male worker for George?

parts.note: far means distant
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A remote man employed by someone called George.
explanation.walkthrough: George comes from Greek 'georgos', a farmer, so a worker for George works for a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer employed on a farm works for a farmer.

clue.text: Unwisely heats large dish

indicators.note: unwisely suggests the letters are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly warms a big serving plate.
explanation.walkthrough: An ashet is a Scottish word for a large oval serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashet is Scots for a large platter for serving meat.

clue.text: Apply restriction as link's not working

parts.note: a tie is a link; the 's stands for is
a computer that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Imposing limits because a connection has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone down is to constrain them.

clue.text: The last thing an old soldier would do?

definitions.text: The last thing an old soldier would do?

parts.words: The last thing an old soldier would do?
parts.note: it recalls the saying that old soldiers never die, they simply vanish gradually

explanation.walkthrough: The song says 'Old soldiers never die, they simply fade away', famously quoted by General MacArthur.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade away is to disappear slowly, which the saying gives as an old soldier's end.

clue.text: High-flying stewardess in near disaster?

parts.note: high-flying things are in the air
a stewardess is a young woman, a miss

explanation.surface: A flight attendant at altitude is involved in a near collision.
explanation.definitionFit: An air miss is an incident where aircraft come dangerously close to colliding.

clue.text: Not forthcoming about Liberal editor being filled to excess

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reticent word goes round the party letter

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details

explanation.surface: A reticent Liberal journalist who has had too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloyed means sickened by too much of something sweet or rich.

clue.text: Meant to change gold cloak

indicators.note: to change means the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Intending to swap a golden cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteau is a loose cloak or gown.

clue.text: Measure taken in Us city to get a girl

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the measure goes within the city letters

parts.note: NY is New York
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Someone measured in an American city to meet a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelly is a woman's name.

clue.text: Biased friend suppresses pictures by one

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so the friend word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend
pictures are art
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A partisan friend hides paintings by a single artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means favouring one side, prejudiced.

clue.text: Philosopher not on for some soldiers

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out of the soldiers word

parts.note: a platoon is a small group of soldiers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker not in favour of a few troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Universal skill not displayed by the angular?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, angular people are not round in shape, so cannot show roundness

explanation.definitionFit: All-round ability is versatility; the second reading jokes that angular figures lack roundness.

clue.text: Longing to get in river? Then you'd need this

indicators.note: the river letter gets inside the word for longing

parts.note: dying for something is longing for it

explanation.surface: If you are so keen to jump into a river, you will need a towel afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: after a dip in a river you need drying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wet from a swim needs towelling off.

clue.text: Cuts fish daughter finds unsymmetrical

parts.note: lops means cuts off
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A girl discovers the fish has been cut unevenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided means uneven, heavier on one side.
